content: Trifectant is a proprietary name for a highly effective, multi-purpose disinfectant. This solution is widely utilized in various settings, including hospitals, laboratories, nursing homes, funeral homes, and medical, dental, and veterinary facilities. It is also employed in any environment where pathogen control is essential. Its applications include cleaning hazardous spills, disinfecting surfaces, sanitizing fabrics, and soaking equipment. Trifectant exhibits an extensive spectrum of antimicrobial activity, effectively targeting viruses, fungi, bacterial spores, and bacteria, including mycobacteria such as Mycobacterium tuberculosis. It is also proven to be effective against pathogens like SARS and avian influenza. However, for optimal efficacy, the solution must be generously applied to a surface and allowed to remain for at least two minutes before being wiped off. Alternatively, items should be soaked in the solution for a minimum of two minutes. The disinfectant contains several active and auxiliary components, including a 5% disinfecting and cleaning agent, sodium hexametaphosphate as a buffering agent, Amaranth dye as a color indicator, and lemon extract as an odorant. The disinfecting agents and detergents work synergistically to combat pathogens. Trifectant is most commonly available in the form of yellow tablets or powder, which dissolve readily in water at concentrations typically ranging from 10 to 30 grams per liter. The yellow coloration of the solution serves as a visual indicator to help gauge the concentration during preparation. Additionally, as the solution ages, it undergoes discoloration, signaling when it needs to be replaced. Once prepared, the solution remains stable for approximately five to seven days. The product has a faint lemon scent, though some users may still find the odor unpleasant. While it is relatively safe for skin contact, it can cause eye damage and should not be used as a hand-washing liquid. When purchased in bulk, Trifectant costs approximately 35 US cents per liter to produce, making it comparable in cost to most bleach-based disinfectants. However, some facilities opt to produce their own alternative disinfectants to reduce expenses. Trifectant is a registered trademark of Antec International, a subsidiary of DuPont.
